overview.headline: How Congress drafted, revised and signed the independence declaration

keyPoints.point: Congress appointed a committee of five on June 10 to draft a statement of independence for the colonies.
keyPoints.quote: Congress appointed on June 10 a committee of five to draft a statement of independence for the colonies.

keyPoints.point: Jefferson drafted the statement between June 11 and 28 after submitting drafts to Adams and Franklin for changes.
keyPoints.quote: Jefferson drafted the statement between June 11 and 28, submitted drafts to Adams and Franklin who made some changes

keyPoints.point: The Continental Congress adopted the Declaration on July 4 1776 after completing revisions.
keyPoints.quote: The Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776.

keyPoints.point: Congress ordered on July 19 that the Declaration be engrossed on parchment with a new title for signing.
keyPoints.quote: On July 19th, Congress ordered that the Declaration be engrossed on parchment with a new title,

keyPoints.point: Although not all delegates were present on August 2, 56 delegates eventually signed the engrossed document.
keyPoints.quote: Although all delegates were not present on August 2nd, 56 delegates eventually signed the document.

keyTerms.gloss: governing body that adopted the Declaration on July 4
keyTerms.quote: The Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776.

keyTerms.gloss: group appointed to draft a statement of independence for the colonies
keyTerms.quote: Congress appointed on June 10 a committee of five to draft a statement of independence for the colonies.

keyTerms.gloss: copied in large hand on parchment for delegates to sign
keyTerms.quote: It was engrossed on parchment and on August 2, 1776, delegates began signing it.

keyTerms.gloss: process of copying a document in a large hand
keyTerms.quote: Engrossing is the process of copying an official document in a large hand.
